key_features.classic_presentation: ONSET: Hours to days, progressive worsening. LOCATION: Chest (dyspnea), bilateral lower extremities (edema). DURATION: Progressive, continuous dyspnea. CHARACTER: Dyspnea, orthopnea (can't lie flat), paroxysmal nocturnal dyspnea (wake up gasping). AGGRAVATING: Lying flat, exertion, fluid intake. RELIEVING: Sitting upright, diuretics. TIMING: Progressive, worse at night. SEVERITY: Severe dyspnea, patient speaks in short phrases. KEY POSITIVES: Bilateral leg swelling, weight gain, pink frothy sputum, rales on lung exam, elevated JVP, S3 gallop. KEY NEGATIVES: NOT unilateral leg swelling (DVT), NOT pleuritic (PE).

red_flags: Rapid weight gain (>5 lbs in days)
History of heart failure or myocardial infarction (MI)
